queries: RoboCasa/LIBERO/BEHAVIOR pick-place of lidded containers (no loose-lid carry found in titles)

nearest_prs.assessment: Accepted (other team): shelve a carton of cans whose untaped bottom flaps open unless held from below. Same family (grip chosen so an unsecured closure stays shut while shelving) but different object and contact: support under the base vs pinch on the walls below a loose top lid. Highest duplicate risk; a reviewer may call ours a variant.

Final rejected (other team): latch a toolbox before carrying it by its lid handle. Rejected as non-robotic noticing plus ordinary moves and not core job work. Ours has no latch to close; the difficulty is the grasp location. Same objection on importance may apply; pitched as Societal relatability instead of jobs.
Accepted: release a two-latch lid and lift it out with both hands. Opening a lid, not carrying a box with its lid on.
Accepted: carry a stack of three boxes onto a shelf squeezed between both arms. Bimanual carry, no loose lid.
Pending: put a toolbox down without blocking an extinguisher. Placement-location rule, different skill.
Revising: close a telescoping-lid box over its product. Closing, not carrying.
Pending (other team): lift an iPhone box's close-fitting lid off slowly. Removing a lid, not carrying a box with its lid kept on; different skill.
Pending: load lidded cups into a drink carrier upright. Placement of cups, lids are fixed; different skill.

physical_skill: Grip a long 1.2 kg tin by its own walls in the 4.5 cm band below a loose, off-centre lift-off lid (with two arms, or one exactly at the middle), carry it level onto a shelf without the lid sliding off or the tin tilting past 30 degrees, set it flat and release clear.
valid_shortcuts: One gripper exactly at the tin's middle can carry it (sags about 8 degrees) and score 1.0; this is a valid route, not penalised.
Sliding or pushing the tin is allowed if the lid stays on and the tin ends flat on the shelf; lifting is needed anyway because the shelf is 3 cm high.
Lifting the lid off and putting it back fails, as the instruction forbids taking the lid off.
distinct_from_nearest: Unlike #1803 (support a flapped carton bottom from below), the closure here is a loose top lid and the forced choice is where on the walls to pinch, below the lid edge and near the ends for balance; unlike #576 there is no latch to work and the instruction does not mention the lid's state. Known risk: reviewers may judge it a variant of #1803 or ordinary carrying.
